headline: Dementia assessments take more than five times as long as the law allows
deck: State auditors sharply criticise the regions; patients in Zealand wait 244 days on average.
standard: In recent years 84 per cent of patients due a dementia assessment have waited longer than the 30 days the law allows, according to a report by Rigsrevisionen, the national audit office. The regions, which run Denmark's hospitals, took 165 days on average last year: 133 in Southern Denmark and 244 in Zealand.

Statsrevisorerne, who check that the state spends taxpayers' money properly, gave the regions the second-sharpest criticism on their scale. They also faulted the 24 days that patients from strong social backgrounds gain over those from weak ones.

Mads Duedahl, chairman of Danske Regioner, the regions' association, calls the criticism justified and says the field must be 'rethought'. The regions want family doctors to do more of the assessments.
